sm: The host opens with a historical footnote: in the 1870s Karl Marx grew fed up with French socialists who called themselves Marxists, and he reportedly said that he was not a Marxist himself. He says the same thing has now happened again, this time with climate activism. Greta Thunberg was asked about the Fridays for Future protest in Berlin, which still meets every week eight years after it began in the Swedish parliament. She burst into open laughter and asked whether they still do that. The host calls it the nail in the coffin of the climate movement and imagines how true believers must feel.

He plays 2019 footage of young strikers with signs like there is no planet B and says they were indulging a delusional fantasy that the world would end because it is a few degrees warmer. He argues that humanity is still here seven years later. He says deaths from climate-related disasters are declining and global wildfire area dropped about 25 percent between 2001 and 2020. He says the people who kept protesting will never admit the movement was wrong, and he turns to what he calls the greatest hits of failed climate predictions, including banned airplanes and gas stoves and repeated new deadlines for the end of the world.

He walks through old predictions, including a 2006 claim that Manhattan would flood, a Pentagon warning from 2004, and a 1989 report of a ten year window to solve the greenhouse effect. He plays a Leonard Nimoy segment and clips from the 1970s warning of a coming ice age after brutal winters. He then plays 1980 and 1983 broadcasts predicting melting ice caps and flooded coastal cities from carbon dioxide, and notes James Hansen's 1988 Senate testimony. He closes by saying snowstorms and cold weather repeatedly embarrassed activists, such as snowed-in Greenpeace trucks, and that activists answered that weather is not climate, which he says makes no sense if CO2 is heating the whole planet.

The host says Greenpeace and others abandoned the term global warming, and that Greenpeace's 2009 annual report used climate change about 44 times and global warming only four. He says he checked Greenpeace's archives and found global warming used far more in earlier reports, such as 1994, before climate change replaced it. He cites a 2002 memo from Republican pollster Frank Luntz, reported by the Guardian, that urged Republicans to drop the phrase global warming. He argues the right did not push back, so a figure like Greta Thunberg, a child who was hard to criticize, was elevated, and critics of her were ostracized.

He plays her famous how dare you speech at the United Nations and says it was theatrical nonsense that the elites ignored. He argues the cause has been on life support and is now flatlined, citing Greta's laughter. He then recounts embarrassing protest moments, including Extinction Rebellion activists blocking a London train station and being dragged off by angry commuters. He plays a 2023 clip in which an official says blockading ambulances amounts to attempted murder. He also shows a driver who plowed through a climate blockade and notes that the group Climate Defiance complained about it online.

The host says the climate movement keeps embarrassing itself and turning the public against it. He plays coverage of the 2023 U.S. Open women's semifinal, where protesters glued their feet to the stands and disrupted play, and says the broadcasters refused to air footage of the demonstrators. He jokes that it was not exactly a Spartacus moment for the climate cult. He also shows a Harvard clip in which activists harassed Senator Joe Manchin, and he says harassing politicians has been a common tactic.

Looking at the bigger picture, he says most people who joined the movement have simply moved on to new causes, as happened with COVID, racial protests and other trends, leaving only a small number of die-hards. He says these followers are not real political adversaries but people who will adopt any new pretext, however absurd or hypocritical. He says Greta effectively admitted the cause is dead and was mocking her own followers. He concludes that, given recent outages, cyber attacks and dire warnings, the next opportunity for them to turn rabid is already here, then wishes listeners a good weekend.
